\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{آتش} \fa{سوزی} (âtash suzi)}{آتش سوزی (âtash suzi)}]{\fa{آتش} \fa{سوزی} (âtash suzi) — a fire, a blaze}

\label{lesson:FA-C328-atash-suzi}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to survive, then the Persian for a lifeguard.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{آتش} \fa{سوزی}}
\textbf{\fa{آتش} \fa{سوزی}} (\emph{âtash suzi}) — \textquotedblleft{}a fire, a blaze\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{دیشب} \fa{در} \fa{یک} \fa{انبار} \fa{آتش} \fa{سوزی} \fa{شد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Dishab dar yek anbâr âtash suzi shod.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Last night there was a fire in a warehouse.
\end{quote}

\emph{âtash} \textquotedblleft{}fire\textquotedblright{} + \emph{suzi} \textquotedblleft{}burning\textquotedblright{}, from \emph{suz-}, the present stem of \emph{sukhtan} \textquotedblleft{}to burn\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{âtash} \textquotedblleft{}fire\textquotedblright{} is inherited from Middle Persian (EtymDB), and \emph{suzi} \textquotedblleft{}burning\textquotedblright{} comes from \emph{suz-}, the present stem of the native verb \emph{sukhtan} \textquotedblleft{}to burn\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{âtash suzi}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{âtash suzi}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{âtash suzi}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for to survive, then the Persian for a lifeguard, then say \emph{âtash suzi} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \fa{آتش} \fa{سوزی} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A fire, a blaze\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{آتش} \fa{گرفتن} (âtash gereftan)}{آتش گرفتن (âtash gereftan)}]{\fa{آتش} \fa{گرفتن} (âtash gereftan) — to catch fire}

\label{lesson:FA-C328-atash-gereftan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a lifeguard, then the Persian for a fire.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{آتش} \fa{گرفتن}}
\textbf{\fa{آتش} \fa{گرفتن}} (\emph{âtash gereftan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to catch fire\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{آشپزخانه} \fa{ناگهان} \fa{آتش} \fa{گرفت}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Âshpazkhâne nâgahân âtash gereft.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The kitchen suddenly caught fire.
\end{quote}

Present \emph{âtash migirad}. \emph{Âtash zadan} is \textquotedblleft{}to set on fire\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{âtash} \textquotedblleft{}fire\textquotedblright{} is inherited from Middle Persian (EtymDB); \emph{gereftan} \textquotedblleft{}to take\textquotedblright{} is inherited too, from the Old Persian root \emph{grab-} \textquotedblleft{}to seize\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{شعله} (sho'le)}{شعله (sho'le)}]{\fa{شعله} (sho'le) — a flame}

\label{lesson:FA-C328-shole}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a fire, then the Persian for to catch fire.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{شعله}}
\textbf{\fa{شعله}} (\emph{sho'le}) — \textquotedblleft{}a flame\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{شعله} \fa{ها} \fa{تا} \fa{سقف} \fa{رسید}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Sho'le-hâ tâ saqf resid.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The flames reached the ceiling.
\end{quote}

Plural \emph{sho'le-hâ}. On a cooker, \emph{sho'le-ye gâz} is the burner flame.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{sho'le} is borrowed from Arabic \emph{shu'la}, \textquotedblleft{}flame\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sho'le}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{sho'le}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for a fire, then the Persian for to catch fire, then say \emph{sho'le} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{دود} (dud)}{دود (dud)}]{\fa{دود} (dud) — smoke}

\label{lesson:FA-C328-dud}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to catch fire, then the Persian for a flame.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{دود}}
\textbf{\fa{دود}} (\emph{dud}) — \textquotedblleft{}smoke\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{دود} \fa{سیاه} \fa{از} \fa{پنجره} \fa{بیرون} \fa{میآمد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Dud-e siyâh az panjere birun miâmad.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Black smoke was coming out of the window.
\end{quote}

\emph{Dud kardan} \textquotedblleft{}to smoke; to give off smoke\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{dud} is a native Persian word; EtymDB glosses it \textquotedblleft{}smoke; sorrow\textquotedblright{} and lists no parent.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{جرقه} (jaraqe)}{جرقه (jaraqe)}]{\fa{جرقه} (jaraqe) — a spark}

\label{lesson:FA-C328-jaraqe}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a flame, then the Persian for smoke.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{جرقه}}
\textbf{\fa{جرقه}} (\emph{jaraqe}) — \textquotedblleft{}a spark\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{از} \fa{سیم} \fa{برق} \fa{جرقه} \fa{پرید}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Az sim-e barq jaraqe parid.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
A spark flew from the electric wire.
\end{quote}

Also figurative: \emph{jaraqe-ye fekr} \textquotedblleft{}the spark of an idea\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
The origin of \emph{jaraqe} \textquotedblleft{}a spark\textquotedblright{} is not settled, and EtymDB lists no entry.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}
